facts.fact: A national program managed by the Rwanda Space Agency will use Planet's near-daily satellite data to monitor agriculture and food security, as announced by Planet and the Government of Rwanda.

note: Budget line for the Space Program (remote sensing, earth observation, satellite communication) names no farming use of satellite data.

facts.fact: The Rwanda Space Agency's GeoHub, supported by an AFD-backed project, uses satellite images to support sectors including agriculture, and geospatial data is already used to build climate projections informing agriculture and food security policy, per the interweave newsletter.

note: Mentions agriculture only as a general area space technology can support; no farming use of satellite data is stated.
Minister's speech names satellite imagery only as a general data need and as a Zambian company's method; no Rwandan farming use of satellite data is stated.

facts.fact: BMZ Digital.Global says the Rwanda Space Agency, the Ministry of Agriculture, Alliance Bioversity-CIAT and FAIR Forward developed a satellite and AI crop mapping method that is currently being tested in four districts for rice, maize, potatoes and beans.

facts.fact: The UK-funded 2024 project has the UK Office for National Statistics support Rwanda's National Institute of Statistics in integrating Earth Observation techniques and machine learning into agricultural statistics.

facts.fact: UK FCDO reports an active project, started 2024-11-08 and funded at GBP 43,000, in which the UK ONS supports Rwanda's national statistics institute NISR to bring Earth Observation techniques and machine learning into agricultural statistics.

facts.fact: Cenfri says the Rwanda Space Agency processed three years of satellite images into weekly NDVI for just over 6,000 maize plots in a test of identifying underperforming fields; it calls the analysis a step needing refinement.

Digital Earth Africa reports a University of Rwanda graduate's research using Landsat NDVI from its platform, with climate data, to assess crop health in the drought-prone Rwimbogo sector, with field validation still to come.
